architecture.promotionLaw: Durable caller promotion is an explicit Agent cognition action over exact current caller-ingress indexes. The Agent chooses a new successor slot, exact currently-promotable caller indexes, a new attempt identity and a bounded basis. Harness does not choose which caller facts deserve persistence.
architecture.additiveSelectionLaw: Caller promotion extends the current committed WorkingSet mechanically. Existing selected pins are retained exactly and the promoted source pin is added. The Agent is not required to restate hidden current pin identities, and Harness does not reinterpret or replace the existing selection.
architecture.exactBytesLaw: The proposal contains no caller text, summary, source bytes, source digest or semantic memory representation. Harness derives exact promoted bytes only from the durable needs_input caller-ingress authority that was present in the exact Provider request which authored the proposal.
architecture.sourceIdentityLaw: The promoted HarnessWorkingViewSource identity is deterministic over Harness Run identity, needs_input pause sequence, exact caller message indexes and exact selected caller message bytes. The resulting source is stored through ordinary WorkingView-source privacy authority before its exact CAS object identity becomes the promoted pin.
architecture.providerProvenanceLaw: AgentTurnRequest may carry callerIngressRefs mapping each currently promotable callerMessageIndex to its exact requestMessageIndex. Promotion admission requires the proposal indexes to be a subset of those exact refs and verifies that each referenced Provider-request message equals the durable caller-ingress bytes.
architecture.visibilityLaw: Caller-ingress provenance is exposed as Harness execution-control metadata rather than hidden implementation state. DeepSeek is told which caller indexes and Provider message positions are currently promotable, while durable selected user-role messages are explicitly outside that set.
architecture.capabilityLaw: promote_caller_ingress is a dynamic cognition capability. The DeepSeek function is exposed only when callerIngressRefs is non-empty and its JSON schema enumerates the exact currently-promotable indexes. When none remain, the control is withdrawn from the Provider surface rather than left as a knowingly unusable function.
architecture.suppressionLaw: After exact caller indexes are promoted, their caller-overlay copies are suppressed only while the corresponding promoted source remains selected in the current WorkingSet. This is provenance-aware projection suppression, not semantic or textual deduplication. If the Agent drops that promoted pin during the same caller interaction, the still-valid caller ingress reappears.
architecture.repeatPromotionLaw: An exact caller index already represented by a currently-selected promoted source cannot be promoted again into a second durable slot. Re-promotion becomes legal again only if that durable pin is dropped while the underlying caller interaction authority is still active.
architecture.interactionBoundaryLaw: The next needs_input Snapshot still consumes caller interaction authority. Unpromoted caller messages disappear at that boundary; promoted messages remain model-visible only because their new WorkingSet source pin owns durable cognition.
architecture.actionCategoryLaw: Caller-ingress promotion is normalized as cognition state, not an AgentToolCall or Runtime effect. It cannot be mixed with Runtime Tools, Run conclusion, historical recall or an ordinary WorkingSet transition in the same normalized turn and consumes no external Tool-call budget.
architecture.privacyLaw: Exact caller promotion requires model-content authority because both ingress and the resulting WorkingView source are model content. Tool-content authority is not required when no Tool channel participates; Tool-bearing surrounding transcripts retain their normal stricter Tool-content requirements.
architecture.recoveryLaw: A completed Provider promotion proposal survives response loss. Fresh-process resume replays the exact durable Provider result without Provider redispatch, applies the promotion exactly once, and then may begin a distinct successor-cognition Provider turn.
architecture.compatibilityLaw: callerIngressRefs is an optional internal AgentTurnRequest continuity field. Existing requests without the field retain their prior serialization and remain readable. No Ordivon Protocol schema, SQLite schema or recommended public caller API changed.
architecture.nonMemoryLaw: P-C1.11 adds no generic Memory service, Conversation Store, semantic summarizer, embedding index, relevance ranker, automatic promotion policy or automatic recall policy.

behavior.subsetPromotion: A caller interaction contained X=CALLER_X_BLUE_17 and Y=CALLER_Y_EPHEMERAL. The Agent promoted only caller index 0. Continuity created one exact source whose messages were exactly (X,), atomically extended the WorkingSet from [A] to [A,X], and left Y interaction-local. After the next needs_input boundary and a fresh process, X remained once through the durable source, Y was absent, and a new caller Z remained interaction-local.
behavior.noAutoPromotion: A caller message became model-visible and the Agent concluded needs_input without issuing promotion. No new WorkingView source selection occurred, the current WorkingSet remained exactly the predecessor selection, and no extra WorkingSet transaction was written merely because caller content existed.
behavior.invalidIndex: A proposal requested caller index 7 when only index 0 existed. The promotion was rejected as invalid model output and the WorkingSet remained unchanged.
behavior.responseLoss: The Provider durably completed a caller-promotion proposal and the bridge then lost the completion response before the Loop applied it. The WorkingSet remained unchanged at the loss point. A fresh process resumed from the original needs_input Snapshot without caller resend, replayed the durable Provider result, applied the promotion exactly once, then legitimately issued a new successor-cognition Provider turn. providerResultsReplayed equaled 1 and Continuity Doctor remained healthy.
behavior.modelOnlyPrivacy: A no-Tool Run with allow_model_content=true and allow_tool_content=false promoted exact caller ingress into a second WorkingSet pin successfully. The bounded two-model-call test then stopped on model budget, proving promotion itself did not borrow Tool-content authority.
behavior.dropReexposes: The Agent promoted one caller index, then an ordinary WorkingSet transition dropped the promoted pin while the same caller interaction remained active. The promoted-state request showed the caller bytes once through durable cognition; after the drop the same caller bytes appeared once again through caller-ingress authority. The final WorkingSet returned to the baseline pin only.
behavior.repeatRejected: After caller index 0 was promoted and its source remained selected, a second proposal attempted to promote the same index into another slot. The second promotion was rejected and only the first durable promoted pin remained.
behavior.deepseekZeroTool: A deterministic DeepSeek request with Runtime tools empty and remaining Tool calls equal to zero still exposed promote_caller_ingress when one callerIngressRef was present. The raw Provider response normalized to caller-ingress promotion rather than AgentToolCall. Disabling the promotion switch rejected the same control.
behavior.deepseekMixedAction: A deterministic DeepSeek response attempted caller promotion and submit_run_conclusion in the same turn. The Adapter rejected the mixed action before any effect rather than choosing one on the model's behalf.
behavior.deepseekCapabilityWithdrawal: With caller-ingress promotion enabled but callerIngressRefs empty, the DeepSeek request contained callerIngress.promotable=[] and did not contain the promote_caller_ingress function. submit_run_conclusion remained available.

realModelExperiments.round1HiddenPinsCounterexample: The first promotion schema required the Agent to restate retained current WorkingSet pins. One real probe invented a logical_ref/generation/zero digest because pin identities were not model-visible; Harness rejected it. A second probe explicitly stated that source pin identities were not provided/inventable and submitted pins=[], which promoted BLUE-17 but dropped the original task source. This falsified the retained-pins proposal shape.
realModelExperiments.round2AdditiveRepair: The proposal was changed so promotion mechanically extends the current selection. Two live probes then promoted BLUE-17 while preserving both the original task source and the new promoted source without guessing pin identities. This validated additive selection but exposed duplicate model projection because BLUE-17 appeared once as durable source and once as still-active caller ingress.
realModelExperiments.round3DuplicateSuppressionCounterexample: Provenance-aware suppression removed the duplicate caller-overlay copy, so BLUE-17 appeared only once. Real probes nevertheless still attempted repeated promotion because durable WorkingView source messages and caller-ingress messages both used role=user; Harness knew the provenance distinction but the Agent did not. This falsified hidden provenance.
realModelExperiments.round4ProvenanceVisibilityRepair: AgentTurnRequest callerIngressRefs and DeepSeek execution-control metadata made exact promotable caller indexes/positions visible. Two probes promoted BLUE-17 and then saw callerIngress.promotable=[] on the successor turn; both stopped repeated promotion and chose needs_input. The current WorkingSet retained task plus promoted BLUE-17 and Doctor remained healthy.
realModelExperiments.round5EmptyCapabilityCounterexample: Even with promotable=[], some real-model runs still called promote_caller_ingress because the function remained present in the Provider Tool schema. This exposed the same class of revoked-capability friction previously found for Runtime Tools and falsified the idea that metadata alone was enough.
realModelExperiments.round6DynamicCapabilityAndDurableReuse: The promotion function was made dynamic: absent when no caller index was promotable and present only when refs existed, with its index schema enumerating current indexes. In live probes the wire then followed absent -> present for BLUE-17 -> absent after promotion. A separate later-interaction control kept the same Run/Provider but disabled the optional promotion surface for the final query; both probes returned candidate_completed from durable cognition, including one exact summary 'The durably stored launch code from the authoritative caller fact is BLUE-17.' BLUE-17 appeared once in each post-promotion Provider view and Doctor remained healthy.
realModelExperiments.wireLaw: The final live wire exposed promote_caller_ingress only on the caller BLUE-17 turn, withdrew it after promotion, preserved the original task source plus promoted caller source, and later supplied BLUE-17 from the durable WorkingSet after the original caller interaction had ended.

conclusion: P-C1.11 closes the interaction-to-durable cognition gap with an Agent-owned, provenance-bound promotion primitive rather than automatic memory. The final law is additive: the Agent selects exact currently-promotable caller indexes and a new slot; Harness derives the exact bytes from the Provider-visible caller ingress, deterministically materializes one source, and mechanically extends the current selected WorkingSet. Real DeepSeek experiments materially changed the design four times: hidden retained-pin identities were removed, duplicate caller projection became provenance-aware suppression, hidden caller provenance became explicit request/control metadata, and unusable promotion capability is now withdrawn when no caller ingress is promotable. A promoted fact survives the next needs_input interaction boundary and can be reused in a later interaction, while unpromoted caller content expires normally. No generic Memory subsystem, semantic promotion policy, Conversation Store, new SQLite schema or public cognition API was required.
knownLimits: Promotion preserves exact caller messages only. P-C1.11 does not summarize, compress, merge, rewrite or semantically normalize caller content before persistence.
Harness proves provenance and exact bytes, not truth. A caller may provide a false fact and an Agent may choose to persist it; the Harness does not become a world-truth verifier.

Harness does not decide whether a caller message is relevant, important or worth retaining. A semantically pointless but structurally valid caller message remains promotable while its caller-ingress authority is active if the Agent chooses it.

The current promotion primitive is additive over the entire current WorkingSet. Replacing or dropping other durable sources remains a separate ordinary Agent WorkingSet transition rather than being folded into promotion.
Promotion currently materializes selected caller indexes together as one WorkingView source under one Agent-chosen slot. It does not expose a semantic record/key-value memory abstraction.

Caller-ingress provenance refs identify exact message positions and interaction indexes; they do not authenticate a human identity, multi-user author or external origin beyond the Harness caller boundary.

Provenance-aware suppression applies only to exact P-C1.11 promoted sources whose evidence validates against the current caller interaction. Harness does not perform generic textual deduplication across unrelated sources.

If a promoted pin is dropped during the same interaction, its caller bytes become visible again because caller authority still exists. After the next needs_input boundary, only independently durable selected sources remain.
The promotion control is currently an opt-in experimental DeepSeek cognition surface. The recommended ordivon_harness.api facade and package root do not expose a new public memory API.
Exact promotion and cross-process replay require model-content retention. Metadata-only continuity can retain fences/digests but cannot reconstruct omitted caller bytes into a WorkingView source.

A later caller query is itself legitimate caller ingress and therefore can be structurally promotable when the promotion surface is enabled. P-C1.11 deliberately does not make Harness infer that a query is unworthy of persistence; provider strategy or a higher-level policy may choose not to grant promotion for that turn.

Real DeepSeek later-interaction completion was demonstrated with the optional promotion surface disabled for the final retrieval turn to isolate durable-reuse capability from the separate semantic choice of whether to promote the new query.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
